chunks.say: What if you built a ladder… all the way to space?
Let's say you climb eight hours a day.
Two hours in, you pass the tallest building on Earth.
Day three. Mount Everest.
Up here, there's only a third of the air.
Without an oxygen tank… you'd already be dying.
Same day, planes fly under your feet.
Minus fifty-six degrees.
Day five. Nineteen kilometers.
Without a pressure suit, the water in your body would start to boil.
Day ten. This is where Felix Baumgartner jumped from a balloon…
and broke the sound barrier on the way down.
Day twenty-five. One hundred kilometers.
Officially… you're in space.
But here's the thing.
Gravity up here is almost as strong as on the ground.
Let go… and you fall all the way back down.
Day one hundred. The Space Station screams past at twenty-eight thousand kilometers an hour.
That's the real trick to staying up here.
Not height… speed.
And if you kept climbing to the Moon?
Two hundred and sixty-three years.
Your great-great-great-grandkids would get there… if they don't look down.
